title: Validating a closed-loop cardiovascular model against real HRV: a whole-record fit reproduces a Fantasia subject's heart-rate variability

dataset.name: Fantasia Database, young healthy subject record f1y03 (ECG beat annotations)
dataset.record: f1y03, 600-beat resting segment @ 250 Hz; mean RR 900 ms, SD 47.5 ms, LF/HF 6.86 (Mayer 0.102 Hz, respiratory 0.178 Hz)
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271:R1078-R1084. PhysioNet doi:10.13026/C21596 (ODC-BY 1.0).

proposition: This is a SIMULATION-VALIDATION case: does the closed-loop cardiovascular state-space model (a damped Mayer oscillator driving the heart period, plus a respiratory RSA term), fit to a REAL RR record by WHOLE-RECORD Bayesian inference, reproduce that record's heart-rate variability? Fitting cardioStateSpace to a real Fantasia RR record (personalizeCardioWaveform, exact Kalman likelihood) yields a stable, physiological fit (damping rho 0.75, interior) that reproduces both the record's overall variability (RR SD 45.8 vs the real 47.5 ms) and its low-/high-frequency autonomic balance (LF/HF 5.98 vs the real 6.86). The model's second-order structure is VALIDATED against reality, distinct from being merely verified on synthetic data (the package tests recover the true parameters from a simulated record).

claims.statement: SD of the real RR-interval series (ms)
SD of RR generated by the fitted closed-loop model (ms)
LF/HF ratio of the real HRV (Mayer vs respiratory power)
LF/HF ratio of the fitted-model HRV

validation.reference: A closed-loop cardiovascular model is VALIDATED (not merely verified) if, fit to a REAL RR record, it reproduces that record's second-order HRV structure: (1) the overall RR VARIABILITY (SD, within ~15%), and (2) the low-/high-frequency AUTONOMIC BALANCE (LF/HF, within ~20%), at a stable physiological fit. The record must carry a genuine, separated Mayer (LF, ~0.1 Hz) rhythm and a respiratory (HF) rhythm, so the Mayer-oscillator + RSA structure applies. Fitting cardioStateSpace to a real Fantasia RR series and comparing the generated HRV must satisfy both.
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia f1y03 (PhysioNet), 600-beat resting RR segment @ 250 Hz
validation.note: This is the L4 (validation-against-reality) tier of simulation validity, distinct from synthetic-data parameter recovery, which only VERIFIES the estimator (the package tests recover g/rho/A_rsa from a simulated record). Fit to the real f1y03 RR record by whole-record Bayesian inference (exact Kalman likelihood + Metropolis), the closed loop reaches a stable, physiological fit (damping rho 0.75, interior -- not railed) that reproduces the record's overall variability (RR SD 45.8 vs 47.5 ms) and its LF/HF autonomic balance (5.98 vs 6.86). Honest scope: (1) what is validated is the SECOND-ORDER (spectral) structure -- the variance and the LF/HF balance -- NOT the exact RR sample path, since HRV is stochastic and a linear-Gaussian model reproduces the spectrum, not the sample path; (2) the model is a LINEAR idealisation -- a single damped Mayer oscillator plus a sinusoidal RSA term -- whereas real HRV is broader-band and messier; (3) the fit has FREE amplitudes (g for LF, A_rsa for HF), so matching the LF/HF ratio is PARTLY structural -- the meaningful content is that ONE stable, interior-damping fit simultaneously reproduces the variance AND the balance from the whole time series at a real record; (4) single record, single segment, and the model does NOT fit every record -- e.g. MIT-BIH record 100 and some Fantasia subjects, whose Mayer/RSA peaks are not separated or whose low-frequency power is too broadband, drive the fit to its parameter bounds. This case lives with PhysioTwin and migrates to public PhysioRecipes.

open_questions.q: A higher-order or nonlinear closed loop (multiple oscillators, a genuine baroreflex delay loop, respiration-driven RSA) fit by particle MCMC/Gibbs would capture the broadband LF structure and the records this linear model rails on; validating across many subjects and conditions (young vs elderly, paced breathing) would map the model's domain of applicability. Documented, not escalated.
